items.title: Language models can rewrite their own weights
items.oneliner: A 27B open model improved on unseen tasks by editing its own weights, pushing training and inference toward collapse.

items.title: AI designed a new CPU architecture
items.oneliner: Frostbite claims an AI-designed, AI-verified CPU with better performance per watt, hinting chip design may automate next.

items.title: A tiny audio model got practical
items.oneliner: Dettato uses 20M parameters yet claims 60x efficiency gains, making on-device audio-to-MIDI suddenly realistic.

items.title: OpenSSL patched a critical overflow
items.oneliner: OpenSSL fixed a CVSS 9.8 buffer overflow in EVP_EncodeBlock(), a reminder that boring primitives still break everything.

items.title: Messaging apps are bracing for AI agents
items.oneliner: Signal is blocking screenshots as OS-level agents spread, and Meta reportedly exposed Signal data during internal testing.

items.title: GrapheneOS says Google is squeezing it
items.oneliner: GrapheneOS alleges Google pressured OEMs and could lock Pixel bootloaders, turning mobile security into a platform control fight.

items.title: The US tightened AI chip exports
items.oneliner: New US export rules hit overseas AI data centers immediately, making compute geography a product constraint, not policy trivia.

items.title: Coding agents reached FPGA territory
items.oneliner: One engineer used coding agents on AWS F2 to build an inference chip prototype and reported a 33x speedup.

items.title: Lovable added safe parallel app drafts
items.oneliner: Lovable now clones app, design, and database into isolated drafts, which is branch previews finally catching up to AI builders.

items.title: ARM improved ASTC texture compression
items.oneliner: ARM added LZ-RDO to astc-encoder, shrinking texture packages with one flag and giving graphics teams free bandwidth back.
